title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff and regional failover under traffic spikes
author: Asha Patel
description: Urgent hotfix to address a regression where the SLO enforcer's backoff ordering and regional failover path could cause cascading load-shedding during brief traffic spikes. Root cause: timer ordering regression introduced in ENG-1823 that allowed multiple backoff windows to be applied out-of-order when regional capacity changed rapidly. This PR introduces deterministic backoff sequencing, adds a quorum guard for regional failover decisions, increases hysteresis on the regional failure detector, and hardens the priority queue draining logic to avoid double-shedding. Includes unit tests and an end-to-end canary in eu-west-1. Checklist: 1) deterministic backoff sequencer implemented; 2) regional quorum guard added; 3) hysteresis tuning + config knobs exposed; 4) additional telemetry for backoff/requeue events; 5) integration tests and canary run passed. Related Linear tickets: ENG-1823, ENG-1840. This is a hotfix and was merged to main with a squash merge after CI re-runs passed.

review_comments: Liam Chen (reviewer): Can you clarify why the sequencer is single-threaded? Will that affect throughput under high QPS?

Asha Patel (author): The sequencer is single-threaded per-enforcer instance to guarantee ordering; throughput is preserved by sharding enforcers across shards — added benchmark and comment explaining tradeoff.
Sophia Morales (reviewer): Suggest adding a small e2e to validate we don't double-shed when a region flaps quickly.
Asha Patel (author): Added integration canary in eu-west-1 and a unit test for rapid region toggle; details included in commits.
Diego Rivera (approver): Verified canary telemetry; observed SLO enforcer latency stable and no extra shedding during 30m spike. Approving for hotfix release.
